stories.title: Missile strikes damage Kyiv bridges as winter approaches
stories.summary: On 16 November, Ukraine hit the Kerch bridge linking Russia to Crimea and launched a wave of missiles and drones that damaged its central road‑bridge arch. Hours later Russia fired seven ballistic missiles at Kyiv, disabling two of the nine bridges that cross the Dnipro River. The war, now over four and a half years, has killed an estimated 100,000 Ukrainian troops and 18,000 civilians, and Kyiv faces freezing nights and frequent blackouts as Russian attacks target electricity generation.
stories.why: Damage to key bridges and power supplies threatens Kyiv’s transport, supply chains and civilian resilience during an approaching winter.

stories.title: Housing shortage dominates Spanish election campaign
stories.summary: Ahead of Spain’s general election on Sunday, housing has become the top concern for voters, with millions protesting nationwide over a shortage of affordable homes. Recent opinion polls suggest the conservative People’s Party is likely to receive the most votes and that the right‑wing Vox party could join the government for the first time, potentially ending Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez’s eight‑year tenure. A BBC interview featured a young couple from Valencia who have been forced to live apart because of high rents.
stories.why: The election will decide which parties set future housing policy, affecting affordability for many Spaniards.
